SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Dysuria (stinging pain on urination) and occasional lower abdominal pain for several days.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms started a few days ago.
- Progression: Not worsening; pain is bothersome but not severe.
- Hematuria: Small amount of blood in urine earlier today.
- Other urinary symptoms: No increased frequency, no flank or back pain, no new urinary discharge.
- Urine odor: Noted as “smells a bit weird,” no significant change in color except for blood noted once.
- Associated symptoms: No fever, no nausea, no vomiting, no diarrhea.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period 2–3 weeks ago; denies possibility of pregnancy; no abnormal vaginal discharge.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with regular partner (boyfriend of two months); uses condoms.
- Previous STD screen: Never had an STD screen.
- Social history: College student studying biology; lives with friends in a flat near college; does not smoke; drinks alcohol socially on weekends.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Past surgical history: Not documented.
- Medications: Tried over-the-counter bicarbonate recently (“dose/route/frequency not documented”); not helping. No regular medications.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (causes swelling—severity not fully detailed, but appears significant).
- Family history: No relevant kidney, bladder, or gastrointestinal issues known.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed or findings documented during this consultation.
- No vital signs available.
- No laboratory or imaging investigations performed or results documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria and Lower Abdominal Pain:
   - Assessment: Likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection (UTI).
   - Differential diagnosis: None documented.
   - Investigations planned: None during current consult.
   - Treatment planned: Prescription for either Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim (dose/route/frequency provided in conversation—one tablet, twice a day, for three days; specific drug choice not specified).
   - Advice: Increase fluid intake; consider drinking cranberry juice. Avoid sexual activity until symptoms clear up. Continue using barrier contraception. Monitor for worsening symptoms (fever, back pain, feeling unwell); advised to return/call if symptoms persist beyond end of week or if new concerning symptoms develop.
   - Referrals: None at this stage.

2. Sexual Health/STI Risk Assessment:
   - Assessment: No overt signs or symptoms of STI, but no prior screening.
   - Investigations planned: None during current consult; opportunity for future well-woman/sexual health review discussed.
   - Treatment planned: None during current consult.
   - Referrals: None at this stage.

Quality checks:

●	Missing but clinically expected elements:
   - Physical examination (abdominal, suprapubic, flank tenderness).
   - Urinalysis (dipstick, microscopy, culture).
   - Allergies: reaction to Clindamycin partially described, but severity/management not fully documented.
   - Medication reconciliation: only current/occasional use described, but not fully exhaustive.
   - Detailed obstetric/gynecologic history (if relevant).
●	No internal conflicts noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, good detail in history, but lacks objective findings/lab data. No physical exam performed or documented. All relevant symptoms discussed.
